shortSummary: Prized tropical timber giant widely grown across South Asian homesteads for lustrous reddish-brown heartwood, woody five-valved capsules, and winged seeds.
leadOverview: Swietenia mahagoni—universally recognized across Bangladesh's villages and roadsides as Mehgoni—is a stately semi-evergreen canopy tree of the Meliaceae family. Celebrated worldwide for fine reddish-brown furniture heartwood, its tall symmetrical crowns also shelter rural homesteads while splitting woody pear-shaped fruits scatter dozens of papery winged seeds across spring winds.

sections.title: Morphological Description
sections.subtitle: Evenly pinnate glossy leaflets, woody pear capsules, and helicopter samara seeds
sections.summary: Anatomy of straight timber trunks, compound foliage, five-parted capsules, and winged seeds.
paragraphs: Swietenia mahagoni develops a tall, straight, buttressed trunk rising 20 to 35 metres beneath a dense rounded dome of glossy deep-green foliage. Young smooth grey bark gradually matures into dark scaly ridges flaking in irregular plates. Leaves are alternate and evenly pinnate (12–25 cm long), bearing 4 to 8 pairs of asymmetrical curved ovate leaflets.

In spring, tiny fragrant greenish-yellow panicles give rise to thick woody, inverted-pear capsules (6–10 cm long) resembling heavy brown eggs suspended upright on sturdy stalks. Upon winter ripening, the five thick woody valves split apart from the base upward, freeing 40 to 50 flat mahogany-brown winged seeds packed tightly around a persistent five-angled woody core.

subblocks.text: Dense interlocking timber core oxidizing from warm salmon-pink when freshly sawn to deep wine-mahogany brown.

subblocks.heading: Paripinnate Leaflets
subblocks.text: Glossy leathery compound leaves flushing bronzed coral briefly after brief dry-winter leaf drop.

subblocks.heading: Woody 5-Valved Capsules
subblocks.text: Heavy erect russet pods splitting upward into five woody petals along a central pentagonal column.

subblocks.heading: Papery Winged Seeds
subblocks.text: Light chestnut-brown samaras (4–5 cm) spiraling downward cleanly in dry winter breezes.

sections.title: Taxonomy & Botanical Classification
sections.subtitle: Sapindales Meliaceae lineage alongside Neem and Big-Leaf Mahogany
sections.summary: Relationship to Swietenia macrophylla and Neem within the mahogany family Meliaceae.
paragraphs: Belonging to order Sapindales and family Meliaceae (the true mahogany family), Swietenia mahagoni shares its fused staminal-tube floral structure and bitter limonoid triterpenoid chemistry directly with Neem (Azadirachta indica). Nikolaus Joseph von Jacquin named the genus honoring 18th-century physician Gerard van Swieten.

Across Bangladesh, growers cultivate both compact-leaved West Indian Mahogany (S. mahagoni) and its faster-growing Amazonian cousin Big-Leaf Mahogany (S. macrophylla, often called 'Boro Mehgoni'), along with fertile natural hybrids combining rapid growth with fine grain.

sections.title: Natural Habitat & Global Distribution
sections.subtitle: From West Indies coral hammocks to Bangladesh's foremost agroforestry crop
sections.summary: Caribbean origin and immense popularity along Bengal village borders and Jessore timber belts.
paragraphs: Native to southern Florida, the Bahamas, Cuba, Jamaica, and Hispaniola, Swietenia mahagoni historically anchored coastal hardwood hammocks before heavy 18th-century colonial logging made natural wild stands scarce (now listed as Endangered in its native Caribbean range).

Introduced to South Asia via the Calcutta Botanic Garden in 1795, mahogany adapted remarkably to the Gangetic delta. Today, millions of planted trees line homestead boundaries, rice-field bunds, and rural avenues across Jessore, Barishal, Cumilla, and Tangail—making Bangladesh one of the world's largest cultivated mahogany reservoirs.

sections.title: Ecological Role & Pollinator Interactions
sections.subtitle: Wind-gyrating samaras, hoverfly blooms, and storm-buffer homestead shelterbelts
sections.summary: Anemochorous winged seed dispersal, stingless bee pollination, and cyclone windbreaks.
paragraphs: Small pale-green flowers rely on stingless bees, flies, and tiny nocturnal moths for cross-pollination in late spring. Months later, dry northwest breezes liberate hundreds of autorotating winged seeds that helicopter 30 to 60 metres away from shading parent crowns.

Deep anchoring roots and stout woody limbs enable mature homestead mahogany shelterbelts to slow severe Kalboishakhi nor'wester and coastal cyclone gusts, though entomologists recommend mixing mahogany with native species to deter mahogany shoot-borer moths (Hypsipyla robusta).

sections.title: Economic, Culinary & Cultural Importance
sections.subtitle: Heirloom furniture joinery, acoustic instruments, and rural savings trees
sections.summary: Cornerstone of South Asian woodworking economy and smallholder household timber wealth.
paragraphs: True mahogany wood possesses legendary workability—straight-grained, warp-resistant, resonant enough for guitar bodies and pianos, and polishing to a satin reddish-amber sheen prized in heirloom beds, wardrobes, and architectural paneling.

Across rural Bangladesh, planting a row of Mehgoni saplings functions literally as a living savings account ('gachher bank') helping farming families fund higher education, home construction, or agricultural equipment over a 15-to-25-year rotation.

sections.title: Traditional & Scientific Medicinal Properties
sections.subtitle: Swietenine limonoids, bitter seed chemistry, and strict toxicity cautions
sections.summary: Bioactive tetranortriterpenoids in bitter mahogany seeds alongside hepatotoxicity warnings.
paragraphs: Mahogany seeds ('Sky Fruit' / 'Mehgoni Beej') contain intensely bitter limonoid tetranortriterpenoids—including swietenine, swietenolide, and mahoganin—which demonstrate anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and insect-antifeedant activity in laboratory studies.
In rural agro-ecology, crushed mahogany seed oil is increasingly formulated as an eco-friendly botanical spray to deter rice and vegetable pests alongside neem extracts.
sections.safetyNote: Do NOT ingest raw mahogany seeds or unregulated 'Sky Fruit' capsules casually: clinical case reports link concentrated Swietenia seed extracts to acute liver injury (hepatotoxicity) and hypoglycemia.

sections.title: Comprehensive Cultivation & Care Guide
sections.subtitle: Flat-wing seed sowing, shoot-borer prevention, and mixed canopy spacing
sections.summary: Propagating fresh winged seeds and raising straight timber trunks free of shoot borers.
paragraphs: Collect freshly split winged seeds in late Sheet–early Boshonto (February–March), trim off excess papery wing tips if needed, and insert seeds wing-upward at a 45-degree angle in loose sandy nursery beds or polybags (pH 5.8–7.5). Keep moist under 30% shade until seedlings emerge in 14 to 21 days.

Plant out saplings at 3-by-3-metre spacing mixed alongside neem, jackfruit, or legumes rather than dense monocultures—this biodiversity masks young apical buds from Hypsipyla shoot-borer moths and ensures straight vertical trunk growth.

sections.title: Annual Phenology & Six-Season Rhythms
sections.subtitle: Flowering, fruiting, vegetative flush, and Shororitu synchrony
sections.summary: Seasonal cadence across Bengal's six-season cycle (Spring (বসন্ত), Winter (শীত)).
paragraphs: West Indian Mahogany (Swietenia mahagoni) aligns its vegetative flushes, anthesis, and fruit maturation tightly with Bengal's Shororitu photoperiod and monsoon moisture transitions, showing peak biological activity during Spring (বসন্ত), Winter (শীত).

Spring (বসন্ত): Flushes coppery-bronze pinnate leaves alongside tiny greenish-cream floral panicles. Winter (শীত): Heavy woody five-valved capsules split upward from the base, freeing dozens of papery winged samara seeds.

sections.title: Seed Germination Biology & Propagation
sections.subtitle: Dormancy regulation, nursery media, and clonal propagation
sections.summary: Reproductive biology and reliable seed or vegetative propagation techniques for West Indian Mahogany.
paragraphs: West Indian Mahogany (Swietenia mahagoni) combines sexual seed propagation—useful for raising sturdy heterozygous rootstocks—with elite clonal techniques such as veneer grafting, air layering (gootee), and semi-hardwood stem cuttings. Fresh recalcitrant or semi-orthodox seeds typically germinate within 14 to 35 days when depulped and sown in warm organic loam.
Clonal orchards standardize crown architecture, early precocity, and uniform biochemical profiles across generations within Meliaceae.

subblocks.heading: Nursery Seed Protocol
subblocks.text: Depulped seed sown cleanly in 2:1 loam-compost media; high viability when fresh.

subblocks.heading: Clonal Method
subblocks.text: Approach/veneer grafting or monsoon air-layering onto vigorous local rootstocks.

sections.title: Pathology Defense, Vectors & Organic IPM
sections.subtitle: Phytoalexin resilience, fungal prophylaxis, and predator guilds
sections.summary: Biochemical defense mechanisms and low-impact organic IPM guidelines for Swietenia mahagoni.
paragraphs: In humid South Asian and tropical growing belts, West Indian Mahogany (Swietenia mahagoni) relies on secondary terpenoid resins, foliar trichomes, and phytoalexin phenolics as front-line biochemical deterrence against herbivores and opportunistic pathogens. Prolonged monsoon waterlogging or stagnant canopy humidity can nonetheless encourage anthracnose (Colletotrichum spp.), powdery mildew, leaf-spot fungi, or root-zone Pythium.

Organic Integrated Pest Management (IPM) prioritizes preventive airflow pruning, Trichoderma-enriched compost amendments around feeder roots, and targeted cold-pressed Azadirachta indica (neem) oil sprays at dusk to suppress sap-sucking aphids, scale insects, and mealybugs without harming native pollinators.

subblocks.heading: Fungal Management
subblocks.text: Prevent overhead foliar wetness at dusk; maintain canopy aeration and copper/Trichoderma prophylaxis.

subblocks.heading: Organic Pest Control
subblocks.text: Neem kernel emulsion (3–5 ml/L) plus conservation of hoverfly and ladybird predator guilds.

sections.title: Conservation Standing & Climate Resilience
sections.subtitle: Population security, agroforestry corridors, and stress tolerance
sections.summary: Biogeographic conservation standing and climate adaptation traits of West Indian Mahogany.
paragraphs: Across its native and naturalized distribution (Caribbean & Southern Florida (Naturalized in South Asia)), West Indian Mahogany (Swietenia mahagoni) demonstrates strong ecological plasticity across alluvial floodplains, homestead agroforestry plots, and urban biodiversity corridors. While cultivated stands remain broadly secure, landrace genetic erosion, coastal salinity shifts, and wetland drainage threaten wild ecotypes and heritage regional varieties.

Long-term resilience depends on decentralized in-situ homestead stewardship, wetland buffer conservation, and botanical garden germplasm collections preserving drought-, flood-, and salinity-tolerant alleles amid shifting monsoon regimes.

sections.title: Horticultural Spacing, Pruning & Telemetry
sections.subtitle: Plot geometry, canopy shaping, and calibrated soil-climate meters
sections.summary: Calibrated horticultural parameters: pH 5.8 – 7.5, Full Sun / Emergent, and structural spacing guidance.
paragraphs: Optimal managed cultivation of West Indian Mahogany (Swietenia mahagoni) calibrates root-zone chemistry around pH 5.8 – 7.5 inside deep well-drained loam. Providing adequate crown spacing prevents humidity buildup and lets lower shoots capture uniform irradiance across full sun / emergent.

Light corrective pruning immediately after main flowering or harvest periods redirects assimilates into healthy vegetative framework, while moisture scheduling (moderate seasonal) stabilizes root turgor without inducing hypoxia.

sections.title: Evolutionary Genetics & Adaptive Phylogeny
sections.subtitle: Sapindales clade divergence and Meliaceae genomic traits
sections.summary: Phylogenetic placement of genus Swietenia within order Sapindales (Eudicot (Malvids)).
paragraphs: Modern molecular phylogenetics (APG IV) places Swietenia mahagoni inside family Meliaceae (মেলিয়াসি (মেহগনি-নিম গোত্র)), order Sapindales, clade Eudicot (Malvids). Drought-resilient timber and medicinal trees of the mahogany order featuring pinnately compound foliage and bitter insect-repellent limonoid triterpenoids.

Within genus Swietenia, specialized morphological adaptations—such as imparipinnate drooping foliage with asymmetrical falcate leaflets—reflect co-evolutionary specialization with regional pollinator guilds and abiotic habitat filters.

sections.title: Field Identification Key & Diagnostic Checks
sections.subtitle: Macro-morphological verification against look-alike taxa
sections.summary: Rapid field-sheet checklist for confirming Swietenia mahagoni (Mehgoni (মেহগনি)).
paragraphs: Field verification of West Indian Mahogany (Swietenia mahagoni) rests on recognizing key Meliaceae family markers: Imparipinnate drooping foliage with asymmetrical falcate leaflets; Staminal tube uniting filaments into a central floral column; Rich azadirachtin and limonoid phytochemistry in seeds and bark. Inspecting fresh leaf arrangement, stem surface texture, and reproductive architecture together eliminates confusion with sympatric congeners.

Straight Red-Heartwood Bole: Dense interlocking timber core oxidizing from warm salmon-pink when freshly sawn to deep wine-mahogany brown. Paripinnate Leaflets: Glossy leathery compound leaves flushing bronzed coral briefly after brief dry-winter leaf drop. Woody 5-Valved Capsules: Heavy erect russet pods splitting upward into five woody petals along a central pentagonal column. Papery Winged Seeds: Light chestnut-brown samaras (4–5 cm) spiraling downward cleanly in dry winter breezes.
